8.text: All these worlds, as said before,¹ are joined by holes situated under the

9.text: Polar Star. Shamans and spirits while going from one world to another slip

10.text: through these holes. The heroes of several tales fly through them while

11.text: riding on an eagle or a thunder-bird. Another way to reach the upper world

12.text: is to go in the direction of the dawn, and ascend a long, steep path that

13.text: leads to the sky. The hero of one tale uses a needle and thread in ascending

14.text: to the upper world. He throws the needle upward, like a dart, and it sticks

15.text: in the sky; then he ascends, using the thread as a rope-ladder. One may

16.text: also ascend to the upper world along the path of the rainbow, or along the

17.text: sun’s rays. The dead ascend to it with the smoke of the funeral pyre.²

18.text: The clouds are also considered a kind of aerial ground upon which one

19.text: may repose while ascending to the sky. In several tales, travellers who

20.text: make a journey upward stop for a night’s rest on the aerial ground of clouds,

21.text: pitching there their tents, and in the morning they continue their journey.
